solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bombshell America's dropped for Iranian revolutionary leaders in Middle Eastern capital …

indicators.note: America is dropped and something else takes its place, signalling a swap of letters

parts.note: a bombshell is a stunner, which slang calls a beaut

indicators.note: the leaders of the two words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A news report: an American bombshell is dropped on a Middle Eastern city as Iran's revolution unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombshell' is not an explosive but a beauty, slang BEAUT; its A (America) gives way to IR, the initials of 'Iranian revolutionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital city of Lebanon, on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Bowled, quickly try to escape dismissal

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
to rush off is to leave in a hurry

explanation.surface: A batsman, bowled, hurries off after his dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'dismissal' look like a batsman's; it is a curt rejection.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt rejection or snub is a dismissal of someone.

clue.text: Popular Conservative Opposition leader got in crookedly, concealing true identity

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the leader of the word is its first letter
crookedly says the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A popular Tory gets into office crookedly while hiding who he really is.
explanation.definitionFit: Going about in disguise or under an assumed name means hiding one's identity.

clue.text: Not quite there, as tomorrow's news is by end of today?

parts.note: tomorrow's newspapers have not yet been read by anyone

indicators.note: the end of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A musing that tomorrow's news, as the day closes, is not quite here yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not quite there is not yet prepared.

clue.text: … a little bit like the US did in 1980?

parts.note: what American voters did at the polls was to choose a president by ballot
the man chosen in that year's presidential race was Ronald Reagan, known as Ron

explanation.surface: A continuation of the previous clue, wondering whether something small resembles America's choice in the 1980 presidential election.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 1 Across; 1980 is when the US elected Ronald Reagan, giving ELECT RON.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle is about as small a bit of matter as there is.

clue.text: Workers organised in contraction?

definitions.meaning: trade unions and socialist parties together representing working people
a contraction of the womb during childbirth is literally a movement of labour

explanation.surface: Wondering whether organised labour is shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names organised labour politics, and punningly a muscle spasm in childbirth.

clue.text: Eddy's dropped right into shaft below — who's to blame?

indicators.note: dropped says the right letter falls from its place in the eddy word
into says the fallen letter lands inside the shaft word
in a down clue, below places the shaft after the eddy

parts.note: a curl of water or smoke is an eddy
a pit is a mine shaft

explanation.surface: A man named Eddy has fallen down a shaft, prompting the question of fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a name but is a swirl, CURL; its R drops down into PIT below.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilty party is the one at fault for an accident.

clue.text: Flipping puzzle has no answer — start again!

indicators.note: has no says the answer's letter is missing from it
flipping turns the puzzle word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle

explanation.surface: An exasperated solver finds the wretched puzzle unsolvable and wants to begin again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse but is the reversal signal: TEASER reversed is RESAET.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a device back to zero is to begin afresh.

clue.text: What's gained by wicked soldiers in gun emplacement

indicators.note: in puts the soldiers inside the emplacement

parts.note: a machine-gun nest is a gun emplacement
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Wicked soldiers occupy a gun emplacement and gain something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to the saying 'there's no peace for the wicked'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the wicked never get respite, so that is all they gain.

clue.text: Two cricket sides divided over the tea — good one's put out just in case

indicators.note: the two sides are split, with the word the sitting over the gap between them

parts.note: the two halves of a cricket field are the on side and the off side
cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: put out says the one is removed from the word for good

parts.note: nice means good or pleasant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cricket match interrupted at tea, with a good batsman given out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into on and off sides; THE splits them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the off chance means doing it in case it turns out useful.

clue.text: Source of pain for non-Home Counties devotee in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
non- here says the Home Counties are left out of the devotee

parts.note: a religious devotee may live apart as a hermit or recluse
the Home Counties lie in the South East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A devotee withdrawing from the area around London is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retreat' fits a recluse so well that it seems part of the picture, but it is the reversal signal; RECLU turned round gives the answer. The Home Counties are the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomach or mouth sore is a painful lesion, so it is a source of pain.

clue.text: No good rules being broken by drug dispenser

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled in another order
no good means the letter for good is absent from the word being

explanation.surface: Rules being broken by a drug dispenser are no good: a pharmacy scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: BEIN (being without its G) and RULES are rearranged together under 'broken'.
explanation.definitionFit: This device turns liquid medicine into a fine mist to be inhaled, so it delivers drugs.

clue.text: If so, perhaps ass was a humbug?

parts.note: on the pattern the clue sets, the ass stands for another farm beast, the pig
in the clue, A is the initial of ass; in the matching pattern the letter is the pig's initial

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some donkey was a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works by analogy: 'ass was a' pairs an animal with its own initial, and the answer does the same with a different animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Humbug and this word both mean nonsense or insincere talk.

clue.text: Chatter inanely during American hikes

indicators.note: during puts the chattering within the American abbreviation

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly at length

explanation.surface: Someone babbles on while an American walks the trails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hikes' looks like walks but is the verb for raising prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To hike prices is to raise them, the same as increasing their rate.

clue.text: 'Hot gear from DIY rags' makeover artist

indicators.note: to rag something is to tear it about, so these letters are torn up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A slogan for a makeover artist who turns home-made rags into hot fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rags' looks like part of the picture (Cinderella's rags) but is the anagram signal for HOT GEAR FROM DIY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cinderella the magical godparent transforms rags into a ball gown: a pantomime makeover.

clue.text: Nurse lacking medallions perhaps gets elevation

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse
no means none, lacking
flashy medallions are an example of bling, showy jewellery

explanation.surface: A nurse without her medals still gets promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising someone to the peerage is a lifting in rank, the sense of elevation.

clue.text: Religious figure one considers again, perhaps

definitions.meaning: punningly, a person who deems a second time

explanation.surface: A believer reconsiders a holy figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ is called the saviour who buys back souls; split, the word is one who judges again.

clue.text: Contents of autopsy report? Boy fed with nothing ruined by squalid vice den

indicators.note: ruined says the boy-fed-nothing letters are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: zero, nothing, looks like O

indicators.note: squalid describes the vice den as messed-up, so its letters are reordered too

explanation.surface: A starving boy ruined by a filthy den of vice: a grim case history.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: BOY FED plus O becomes BODYOFE, and VICE DEN becomes VIDENCE. The definition puns on an autopsy report literally being about a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully, a post-mortem report concerns a corpse, yet the phrase means a mass of proof gathered.

clue.text: Daffodil and primrose, say, almost entirely grown facing north at bottom of yard

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed word sits beneath the yard's letter
in a down clue, facing north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed
almost entirely means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: swollen means grown larger

explanation.surface: Spring flowers almost fully grown, turned towards the north at the far end of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The flowers seem to be what's in the yard, but daffodil and primrose here are shades of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodil and primrose are both names of pale hues of that colour.

clue.text: Easily led, steered clear of wedding in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the phrase is to be heard, not read

parts.note: ducked the aisle means avoided walking up it to be married

explanation.surface: Someone easily persuaded avoided getting married, as they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliable metal can be drawn out; figuratively a pliable person is easily influenced.

clue.text: Sound of wind in trees Sebastian recorded for thriller

indicators.note: recorded says the words are heard as spoken

parts.words: Sound of wind in trees Sebastian
parts.note: wind in the trees can sigh, and Sebastian Coe is the British Olympic runner

explanation.surface: A recording of breezes in woodland made by a Sebastian, used for a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is a British Olympic middle-distance champion, later Lord Coe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1960 film is a classic suspense thriller.

clue.text: In school, pupil's leaving to suppress gurgling sound

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the abbreviation for school
leaving means the pupil's letter departs from the word for suppress

parts.note: to quell is to put down or suppress
L for learner, a pupil, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: At school, a departing pupil tries to stifle a gurgle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To suppress' looks like the definition; it gives QUELL, and the definition is the sound at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The sucking noise of boots in mud is exactly that wet gurgling noise.

clue.text: Loose woman relative removing top

indicators.note: removing top drops the first letter, the top in a down entry

parts.note: an auntie is a female relative

explanation.surface: A promiscuous female relative strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose woman' reads as one phrase; 'Loose' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot is to unfasten it, the sense of undo.

clue.text: Ghastly old woman to be concerned about bachelor

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old woman

indicators.note: about says the caring word goes round the bachelor's letter

parts.note: to care is to be concerned

explanation.surface: A mother worried over her unmarried son, to a ghastly degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grim and gruesome, especially concerned with death, is ghastly.

clue.text: Shave for the first time? Don't use so much

definitions.meaning: a first shave removes a youth's fluffy facial growth, punningly
to reduce one's consumption of something

explanation.surface: A boy's first shave, and advice to economise.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is shearing off soft fluff; idiomatically it means reducing consumption.

clue.text: Expression that's foolish — 'Time is money'

indicators.note: the quotation says time becomes money, so one letter turns into the other

parts.note: someone foolish is an idiot

explanation.surface: Dismissing the proverb 'time is money' as a foolish saying.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted proverb is the instruction: in IDIOT, the T for time becomes M for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed phrase whose meaning is not literal, like a proverb, is a turn of phrase.

clue.text: One supervising old poet's output in front of Queen

indicators.note: in front of places the poetry before the royal letters

parts.note: a poet produces verse
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: An old poet's work is presented before the Queen by an official.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor or foreman watches over others' work.

clue.text: Severe gremlins hold back business deal

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read from right to left
the two words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: Nasty little gremlins stall a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Two companies combining into one is a kind of business transaction.
